text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said the government will launch a campaign agaist those who avoid paying taxes.
- Deputy finance minister Rimas Survila, elected chairman of Lithuania's Savings Bank council, has not repaid a 14,600 litas debt to the central bank, the Bank of Lithuania.
- New Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta was sworn in before parliament.
- Parliament started the dismissal process for Prosecutor General Vladas Nikitinas.
- 23 candidates will compete for four vacant seats in parliament, which will be held together with the local elections on March 23.
- Uzbekistan supports Lithuania's aim of joining NATO.
- Butinge oil terminal is a question of national security and parliament did not come to an agreement on boosting the share capital to 240 million litas.
- The present debt of commercial LNK television is $3.5 million, bigger than its assets.

- Siemens director general for Lithuania Yrjo Kamarainen appologised in a letter to the prime minister over a suggestion by the head of a subsidiary that the litas currency should be devalued and denied rumours that the German company is to quit Lithuania.
- In order for Lietuvos Energija (LE) to work profitably, energy consumers would have to buy 30 percent more electricity. It made a 376.57 million litas loss in 1996.
- Lithuanian banks are waiting for their audited results.
